relations.note: Athtar is commonly reconstructed as Athirat’s son from Ugaritic divine-family context.
Athirat proposes Athtar the Awesome as replacement for absent Baal.
Athtar is reconstructed as El’s son by extension from Athirat’s maternity.
El contextually authorizes or accepts the succession process, though the damaged text is uncertain.

relations.myth: Athtar attempts to occupy Baal’s throne
relations.note: Athtar sits on Baal’s throne, cannot fill it, relinquishes the office, and descends.

relations.myth: Proposed shared residence assigned by El
relations.note: A disputed reconstruction has Athtar assigned to dwell with Yam and Nahar.
Multilingual scribal lists apparently align Athtar with the Hurrian martial god Aštabi.
Athtar and Chemosh form the debated compound deity Ashtar-Chemosh, recipient of Nebo’s devoted population.
A damaged passage pairs Šagar with an Ashtar or Ishtar form without narrative action.
Sabaic inscriptions jointly invoke Athtar and Almaqah for protection or dedication.
Athtar appears with Ḏāt Ḥimyam in invocations protecting dedicants, families, and property.
